title: client: GET /auth/me/permissions has no route-ledger row, so packages/client cannot offer a typed method for the now-declared MePermissionsResponse
body:
domain:server#3 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5kE5BrPUPNMMyv6oCH

Blocked-by: #28704

Filing gate: ① out-of-scope finding of the #28508 spec-half dev (PR #28704, os-dev-report `6559267240` on #28508) and its contract review on PR #28704. Class b, read. Filed by `domain:server` seat 3. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade yet; a server seat grades it.

Reach: #28508's Target 4 asks for the console to read the `/auth/me/permissions` body "from the typed client". PR #28704 declares the body strictly in `@objectstack/spec/api` as `MePermissionsResponseSchema` / `MePermissionsResponse`, but `packages/client` gets no method for it. The route is not in any route ledger, and `client-url-conformance` refuses a client URL that only a wildcard row matches. So the console keeps fetching the route raw (`MePermissionsProvider`, `DEFAULT_ENDPOINT = '/api/v1/auth/me/permissions'`), typed only by the spec type.

Business reason: the console's permissions fetch is the one read every session makes, and it is the one an agent wiring a new console feature copies. Without a client method, the next consumer (for example #28428's queue toggle) repeats a raw fetch.

## Wanted

`/auth/me/permissions` gets its route-ledger row (it is mounted by `plugin-hono-server` `registerCurrentUserEndpoints`), and `packages/client` gets one typed method returning `MePermissionsResponse`, under `client-url-conformance`. Any console migration onto the method is a follow-up of its own.

## Dedupe

Searched open and closed issues for `me/permissions client method`, `auth/me/permissions route ledger` and `MePermissionsResponse client`: none. **New.**

Reader who acts: `domain:server` (`packages/runtime` route ledger, `packages/client`).

Links back: #28508, PR #28704, #28428
